name: Jahmyr Gibbs
injury_now: Sprained MCL + back issue cost him most of camp; since practiced fully, cleared for Week 1.
role_note: Montgomery traded away — Gibbs is now the outright bell-cow per Dan Campbell, no committee. New OC Drew Petzing (ex-ARI) replaces Morton; elite supporting cast (Amon-Ra, LaPorta, Goff).
thesis: True bell-cow workload upside now, but an in-camp MCL/back scare and a brand-new OC keep this from being zero-risk.

name: Bijan Robinson
injury_now: No injury concerns; has never missed an NFL game.
role_note: Allgeier left in FA; Brian Robinson Jr. is a true handcuff not a committee partner, so Bijan's already-massive touch share (366 touches in 2025) should grow. New OC Tommy Rees leaning run-heavy.
thesis: The safest pick of the group — durable, workload about to grow further, offense being built to run through him.

name: Ja'Marr Chase
injury_now: Left knee hyperextension from a practice fall; limited in practice, Zac Taylor optimistic for Week 1 opener.
role_note: Undisputed alpha WR1, led NFL in targets (185) in 2025. Same OC/HC return and full starting O-line back, but it's the league's cheapest/oldest O-line; Burrow has played 10-or-fewer games in 3 of 6 seasons, which is the real threat to Chase's floor.
thesis: Elite target monopoly, but the floor lives and dies with Burrow's O-line-dependent health, not Chase's own minor knee issue.

name: Puka Nacua
injury_now: Psoas/groin soreness limited him through camp, trending to play Week 1. Bigger overhang: unresolved NFL review into an off-field incident (alleged biting/assault claim, plus backlash over a livestream gesture) — no suspension yet but a live possibility.
role_note: Target monster (28.8% share) even alongside Davante Adams; new OC Nate Scheelhaase, same Stafford/McVay infrastructure. Has missed time in 2 of 3 pro seasons already.
thesis: The best per-game fantasy performer at any position in 2025, but recurring injuries plus an unresolved suspension threat make him the true wildcard of the group.

name: Jonathan Taylor
injury_now: Healthy, no designation. Sat preseason finale as precautionary rest; full participant heading into Week 1.
role_note: Led NFL in carries (323) and rushing TDs (18) in 2025, 70%+ snaps almost every game, minimal committee threat. O-line upgraded (new C, new RT). Taylor was RB2/game with Daniel Jones healthy but fell to RB22/game after Jones' Achilles injury — backup QB play is the swing factor.
thesis: Elite three-down volume on an improved O-line makes Taylor a 1.01-1.03 caliber pick as long as Daniel Jones stays upright.

name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
injury_now: No Week 1 designation; only recent note is a same-game-return concussion evaluation in the Feb 2026 Super Bowl. Clean bill of health entering camp.
role_note: Locked in as clear WR1 with a league-leading 33.9% target share (119/163 targets, 1,793 yds, 10 TD) under Kubiak's scheme. Kubiak left for Raiders HC; Seattle moves to new OC Brian Fleury for 2026 — real scheme-continuity question, though Darnold/Kupp/corps return intact.
thesis: A proven, injury-free elite target hog whose only real 2026 risk is an unproven new OC after Kubiak's departure.

name: Christian McCaffrey
injury_now: Calf tightness sidelined him for stretches of camp/preseason (workload management, not a re-aggravation); back to full practice, likely Week 1 starter but some outlets still list him questionable.
role_note: Bounced back from a 13-game-missed 2024 (Achilles tendonitis + PCL sprain) to lead the NFL in touches (413) in 2025. For 2026 the 49ers are explicitly managing his workload with Jordan James/Kaelon Black to avoid a repeat breakdown — team-level caution given he's now 30.
thesis: Best floor in football when healthy, but a three-year pattern of major leg injuries plus a fresh camp calf scare and an explicit team plan to reduce his touches make him the highest-variance pick of this group.

name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
injury_now: No current Week 1 concern; only offseason procedure on record is a minor 2025 knee clean-up (already resolved).
role_note: Entrenched slot/high-volume WR1, career-best 172 targets in 2025, third straight season as a top-3 PPR WR. Lions move to a third straight new play-caller in 2026 (Petzing replacing Morton) — real but likely marginal continuity risk given Goff/Gibbs/Williams around him.
thesis: The model of a durable, high-floor target hog; the OC change is real but likely marginal given the talent around him.

name: James Cook III
injury_now: No injury designation heading into Week 1; full practice participant all week. Minor camp ankle/foot soreness resolved.
role_note: Locked into bell-cow role on a top-tier Bills offense; led NFL in rushing yards (1,621) in 2025. Only real competition is Ty Johnson/Ray Davis change-of-pace. New OC Pete Carmichael (reunited with Joe Brady) signaling a bigger receiving role for 2026 — passing-game usage had been thin (8% target share).
thesis: A locked-in workhorse on the league's best offense with a real shot at expanded passing-game touches — one of the safest RB1 bets available.

name: CeeDee Lamb
injury_now: Cleared and healthy — no shoulder or ankle issue reported; full participant in August 2026 camp, on track for Week 1.
role_note: Still Dallas's clear WR1 and focal point (25.7% target share) but must fend off a crowded WR room (Pickens added) for volume; Dak's O-line remains shaky (Zack Martin retired, Guyton unproven at LT). 2025 total hurt by missed games and bad TD luck (8 red-zone looks, 3 scores).
thesis: Target share and talent are still elite, but two straight seasons of missed time make him a high-ceiling WR1 with real recent-injury risk baked in.

name: Justin Jefferson
injury_now: Mild hamstring strain in August 2026 camp (~3 weeks out) but has returned to full practice, on track for Week 1.
finish_2025: WR21 total / capped by QB carousel
role_note: Still the clear alpha and target hog regardless of QB; 2025 production capped by a QB carousel (McCarthy/Wentz/Brosmer) and a TD famine (2 actual vs. ~8.8 expected). Kevin O'Connell has now named veteran Kyler Murray the Week 1 starter — a real QB upgrade over last year's revolving door.
thesis: A target monster whose 2025 dud was almost entirely a QB problem — an actual veteran starter plus a clean bill of health makes him a bounce-back WR1 with a recent hamstring flare-up as the only real caveat.

name: De'Von Achane
injury_now: Missed final two preseason games/practice with a calf injury (held out as preventative); GM/coaches say on track for Week 1 and Achane says he feels 100 percent. Also had offseason shoulder surgery, fully participated in camp.
role_note: True 3-down bell-cow with elite receiving usage (18.7% target share, 2nd among RBs). Major 2026 upheaval: new HC Jeff Hafley replaces McDaniel, new OC wants a more run-heavy scheme (favorable), but Tua released and Hill/Waddle both gone — receiving corps is thin, increasing Achane's target ceiling but putting more of the offense's overall quality on him.
thesis: Elite per-touch explosiveness and receiving role, but a third straight year of soft-tissue durability flags plus a gutted, coaching-staff-in-flux Miami offense make him the boom/bust pick of the group.

name: Saquon Barkley
injury_now: Tweaked left foot/ankle at Eagles practice Sept 3, 2026 (cleat came off); no formal diagnosis yet, team optimistic it's minor.
role_note: Still the unquestioned bell-cow — carry/snap share rose to ~70%/79% in 2025 — but production dropped from RB1-level 2024 (2,283 yds) to RB14 in 2025, offense-wide decline not usage-driven. New OC Sean Mannion (first-time play-caller) installs more outside zone; O-line a year older and reportedly regressed.
thesis: Elite touch volume in a run-funnel system gives a safe floor, but a green rookie play-caller, a declining O-line, and a fresh ankle/foot tweak cap the ceiling versus his 2024 peak.

name: Derrick Henry
injury_now: Healthy. Minor collision/knee scare at May 2026 OTAs, walked off fine. No Week 1 designation.
role_note: Workhorse role intact (307 carries, 1,595 rush yds, 16 total TDs in 2025). OC Todd Monken left for Browns HC job, replaced by first-time OC Declan Doyle installing a new scheme. No real touch competition (Hill/Ali are change-of-pace only). Signed a 2-yr/$30M extension through 2027.
thesis: Ironman durability and an unchallenged bell-cow role make him one of the safest volume bets in the format, but he's 32 with a brand-new, unproven play-caller — the age cliff is a when-not-if risk.
